To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we provide the first theoretical and modelling framework to describe the dynamic of social networks with heterogeneous propensity of individuals in establishing social ties and in being socially active.

i) the heterogeneous activity and tie-allocation mechanisms can be described in terms of a simple stochastic network model; ii) the Master Equation of the stochastic network model can be solved analytically in the asymptotic regime, providing an explicit description of the dynamical system and its scaling laws; iii) the analytical predictions match with the empirical data.
the evolution of social networks can be modelled as a dynamical system, whose Master Equation can be solved analytically in the asymptotic regime.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of social interactions in temporal networks, with a particular attention on the role played by the heterogeneity in the activity of individuals and in their tie allocation strategies.

the development of a theoretical framework to model social networks and the dynamic of their evolution, with a particular focus on the impact of the heterogeneous activity of the individuals in establishing new social ties.
the development of a general theory for the dynamics of time-varyning networks with heterogeneous activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model can be considered as a good candidate to explain the evolution of the social networks.
we have developed a general theory of social dynamics that can be used to understand, predict and design the evolution of social networks.

the model proposed here provides a rigorous dynamical framework for the evolution of social networks, that can be extended in the future to include additional mechanisms and to generate accurate data driven predictions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a theoretical framework for the evolution of a social network that is driven by the heterogeneous activity and tie-allocation of its members.
we provide an analytical framework for the study of time-vary networks with heterogeneous activity.

we have developed a new theoretical approach for describing the evolution of time-vary social networks that is able to quantitatively reproduce the empirical observations and to generate predictions for the asymptotically scaling behaviour of the systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamic of social networks in the asymptotic time limit can be described and predicted by a simple model that only depends on a few parameters.
the dynamic of social networks can be quantitavely described and predicted by a few dynamical parameters, which can be easily extracted from empirical data.
social networks can be described by means of a few simple mechanisms and their evolution can be described in a rigorous and quantitative way.
